text: When you design a REST API, it is important to follow some best practices. First, give your endpoints clear and meaningful names, and use nouns instead of verbs. For example, use `/users/123` rather than `/getUser?id=123`. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, such as 200 for success, 201 for creation, and 404 when a resource is missing. Third, write good documentation so developers understand how to use your API quickly. Finally, use versioning, like `/v1/users`, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. These simple rules make your API easier to use, maintain, and grow over time.
